docRequirement: hooks.md § ConfigChange binds the event to configuration FILES: "Runs when a configuration file changes during a session" and "ConfigChange hooks fire for changes to settings files, managed policy settings, and skill files" (hooks.md:2360-2364). The input must carry `source` and optionally `file_path` — "In addition to the common input fields, ConfigChange hooks receive `source` and optionally `file_path`. The `source` field indicates which configuration type changed, and `file_path` provides the path to the specific file that was modified" (hooks.md:2398) — where `source` is one of `user_settings`, `project_settings`, `local_settings`, `policy_settings`, `skills` (hooks.md:237, :2363-2371), and that value is what the matcher filters on. A block decision must prevent the change taking effect, except for `policy_settings` (hooks.md:719, :2413).
current:
Nessy emits an event named ConfigChange that fires on a disjoint trigger and carries a different payload.

- Sole emitter: `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:7326-7342` `emitConfigChangeHook(configKeys)`. Payload is exactly `{ hook_event_name: 'ConfigChange', lifecycle_version: 1, config_keys, config_digest }` — no `source`, no `file_path`.
- Its four call sites are all runtime session-config commits, never a file: `pi-agent.ts:6964` and `:6975` (`updateRuntimeConfig`, keys `authType/model/providerType/runtime`), `:6983` (`setModel`, key `model`), `:6999` (`setThinkingLevel`, key `thinkingLevel`).
- Blocking is advisory only: `pi-agent.ts:7331-7341` receipts a `block`/`deny` as `__HOOK_BLOCK__ … applied:false` because "the config has already been committed by the time this fires" (comment at `:7332-7336`).
- Matcher: `packages/shared/src/automations/utils.ts:221-239` — ConfigChange falls into `getMatchValueForSdkInput`'s default branch and returns `''`; the stated reason is at `:229-232` ("Nessy's ConfigChange reports runtime session-config keys (`model`, `authType`, `thinkingLevel`, …), not settings-file sources").
- Registration diagnostic: `packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-automation.ts:346-350` `MATCHER_INERT_AGENT_EVENTS` warns `plugin.hooks.matcher_never_matches` for ConfigChange, so the inertness is surfaced to the hook author but not fixed.
- Contract registry row: `packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:85` — `owner: 'pi-agent'`, `ordering: 'after runtime config commits'`, `redactedPayload: ['config_keys', 'config_digest']`.
- The settings-file watcher that a correct producer would ride ALREADY EXISTS and already fires per-file, but never reaches the hook layer: `packages/shared/src/config/watcher.ts:430-440` (global `<CONFIG_DIR>/config.json`, `preferences.json`, `theme.json`, `hooks.json`), `:466-523` (workspace `permissions.json`, `automations.json`/`hooks.json`/`config.json`, `skills/{slug}/SKILL.md`), `:1017-1024`, `:1029-1033`. Its consumers in `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:6940-7025` reload and broadcast only — `onAutomationsConfigChange:6978`, `onUserGlobalHooksConfigChange:6996`, `onDefaultPermissionsChange:7010`, `onSkillsListChange:7014`, `onSkillChange:7018` emit no hook event. The one callback that DOES dispatch an automation event, `onLabelConfigChange:6967-6976` → `automationSystem.emitLabelConfigChange()` (`packages/shared/src/automations/automation-system.ts:598-603`), is a Nessy-native `LabelConfigChange`, a different event.
- Managed policy has no emitter either: `packages/shared/src/config/managed-delivery.ts:61-62`, `:187`, `:732` fetch and refresh managed settings from the gateway with no ConfigChange emission.
- The payload TYPE is already sufficient: `SdkAutomationInput.source?: string` (`packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:754`) and `file_path?: string` (`:820`) exist; `config_keys`/`config_digest` are at `:871-872`. `packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:46-79` already exports the whole input as `NESSY_EVENT_DATA` and maps `input.source` → `NESSY_SOURCE`.
- Current behaviour is locked by two tests: `packages/shared/src/automations/conditions.test.ts:656-669` asserts a `project_settings` matcher on ConfigChange is `false`, and `packages/shared/src/plugins/__tests__/hooks-automation.test.ts:305-325` asserts the `matcher_never_matches` warning for it.
divergence:
Four distinct deltas; only one is a key-name problem.

1. TRIGGER (the real defect). Documented occurrences are settings-file / managed-policy / skill-file changes. Ours are runtime session-config commits (`model`, `authType`, `providerType`, `runtime`, `thinkingLevel`). The two sets are DISJOINT: no settings-file edit produces an occurrence at all, so even `"matcher": "*"` never sees one; and every occurrence we do produce is one the page never describes.

2. PAYLOAD. Documented `source` (required, five-value vocabulary) + optional `file_path`; ours `config_keys: string[]` + `config_digest`. This is NOT a key rename with a right value behind it — the values do not exist anywhere in the process at emit time. Both documented field names already exist on `SdkAutomationInput` (`types.ts:754`, `:820`) and are simply never set for this event, so this is a producer gap, not a schema gap.

3. MATCHER. `getMatchValueForSdkInput` returning `''` (`utils.ts:221-239`) is a CONSEQUENCE of 1+2 and is a recorded, tested, author-diagnosed decision (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-inert-unit-b.md:155-165`) — correct given today's payload, and wrong only once the producer lands. Do not "fix" the matcher on its own: it would then read a field nothing sets.

4. BLOCKING. Documented: a block prevents the change taking effect, except `policy_settings`. Ours: advisory receipt after the change is already committed (`pi-agent.ts:7331-7341`). For the file-driven occurrences the documented semantics ARE reachable — skip the in-memory reload — which the runtime-config path could not do.

blastRadius:
Crosses three packages and one wire boundary.

- `getMatchValueForSdkInput` (`packages/shared/src/automations/utils.ts`) is the single matcher adapter for BOTH backends: `matcherMatchesSdk` → `AutomationSystem.executeAgentEvent` (`automation-system.ts:629`) on the Pi/native path, and `pluginMatcherMatches` → `executePluginHookAutomations` (`packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-automation.ts:326-337`, called from the SDK callback at `:1643-1653`) on the Claude-SDK path. Changing the ConfigChange case changes both at once.
- HOOK-INPUT WIRE BOUNDARY (a risk trigger in this repo): the payload is serialised whole into `NESSY_EVENT_DATA` and onto hook stdin by `buildHookCommandEnv` (`packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:46-79`), and `input.source` already maps to `NESSY_SOURCE` (:66). Third-party hooks imported from Claude and Codex plugins read that JSON; adding `source`/`file_path` is additive but externally observable. No persistence boundary is crossed — nothing is written to disk.
- CROSS-PACKAGE IMPORT: `AGENT_EVENT_CONTRACTS_V1` is re-exported into the Pi subprocess as `PI_LIFECYCLE_HOOK_CONTRACTS` (`packages/pi-agent-server/src/extensions/lifecycle-bridge.ts:3, :25`), so the contract-row edit reaches `packages/pi-agent-server`. `redactedPayload` is documentation-only today (its one consumer is the InstructionsLoaded assertion at `lifecycle-bridge.test.ts:172`), so that part is low risk.
- IMPORTED-PLUGIN PATHS: ConfigChange is a mapped event name for both foreign formats — `packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters.ts:142` and `:161`, `hooks-automation.ts:391`, allowlisted at `packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-runtime.ts:44, :177`, and covered by `packages/shared/src/plugins/__tests__/format-adapters.test.ts:3694`. Claude and Codex plugins can already register ConfigChange hooks, so this changes imported-plugin behaviour, not just native automations.
- DECISION CONTRACT: `packages/shared/src/automations/hook-decision-contract.ts:48` lists ConfigChange as top-level-`decision`, exercised by `hook-decision-contract.test.ts:23, :47, :62` and `packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/hook-block-decisions.test.ts:56`. Touching blockability touches those.
- EXECUTION VOLUME: `ConfigWatcherManager` runs per workspace and watches the workspace dir recursively; a new emitter turns every settings save into a hook run. The existing per-key debounce (`watcher.ts` `debounce()`) coalesces bursts, but editor atomic-rename saves can still produce two events — verify de-duplication, since a hook that spawns a process per save is a real cost.
userImpact:
Concrete and reachable today, on the default Pi runtime.

A user who writes a ConfigChange hook — natively in `hooks.json`, or by installing a Claude plugin that ships one — gets one of two wrong outcomes:

(1) With any documented matcher (`"matcher": "project_settings"`, `user_settings`, `skills`, `policy_settings`, `local_settings`), the hook NEVER runs. Nessy does warn at install/registration time (`plugin.hooks.matcher_never_matches`), so it is not silent, but the hook is dead.

(2) With a catch-all matcher, the hook DOES run — on the wrong occurrences. It fires when the user picks a different model in the composer, changes thinking level, or a connection runtime refreshes; it does NOT fire when they edit `~/.nessy-agent/config.json`, the workspace `hooks.json`/`automations.json`/`permissions.json`, a `SKILL.md`, or when managed gateway settings refresh. The `audit-config-change.sh` recipe printed in hooks.md § ConfigChange therefore writes an audit log with no `source`, no `file_path`, and no settings-file entries at all — it logs model switches instead.

For this fork specifically, the missing occurrence is the one `server-managed-settings.md:277` names as the mechanism to log or block unauthorised changes to managed policy: that tamper-detection path has nothing to fire on. And because the block is advisory (`pi-agent.ts:7331-7341`), even a hook that does fire cannot prevent anything.

UNVERIFIED, and deliberately not load-bearing: whether the upstream Claude Agent SDK itself emits ConfigChange when `NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE` is enabled (off by default). What IS verified is that if it did, our second-pass check in `executePluginHookAutomations` → `matcherMatchesSdk` would still discard a narrowing matcher, because the SDK path re-runs our own matcher (`hooks-automation.ts:1643-1653`).
